name: Viz Studio
description: 118 community visualizations for Looker Studio: KPIs, time series, marketing, distribution, network & more.

components.name: A/B Test Results
components.description: CI bars for A/B variants with significance annotation.
components.shortDescription: See which variant won: confidence intervals and significance, side by side.
components.longDescription: Plots A/B variant means with 95% confidence interval bars and an inline significance annotation, so the verdict isn't buried in a stats table. Built for experimentation reviews where stakeholders need 'did B beat A?' answered in one glance. Cross-filter into individual test cells to inspect cohort-level lift.
useCases: Compare conversion rate between Control and Variant B
Display lift with significance after a 14-day test
Review multiple test cells in a quarterly experimentation digest
Justify a feature rollout with statistical evidence
examples: Checkout button color test: 4.2% vs 5.1% conversion, p<0.05
Onboarding flow A/B/C with lift bands

components.name: Breakdown Chart
components.description: Composite donut ring + horizontal progress bars showing category breakdown distribution. Auto-detects dominant category and highlights it with accent color. Configurable colors, bar sizing, keyword-based category coloring, and cross-filtering.
components.shortDescription: Donut ring + progress bars that surface the dominant category at a glance.
components.longDescription: Composite donut ring and horizontal progress bars showing how a total breaks down by category. Auto-detects the dominant category and highlights it with your accent color. Keyword-based category coloring, configurable bar sizing, theme-default palette, and cross-filtering into the rest of your report.
useCases: Break a KPI down by segment
Highlight the leading category in a mix

components.name: Arc Diagram
components.description: Node-link arc diagram with semi-circular arcs connecting source/target nodes. Supports arc color modes (source, target, single, gradient), node scaling by degree, sort options, hover highlighting, tooltips, and cross-filtering.
components.shortDescription: Pairwise relationships rendered as elegant arcs over a single axis.
components.longDescription: Nodes lined up along a baseline; semi-circular arcs connect related pairs with weight encoded as thickness. Arc color modes (source, target, gradient, single), node sizing by degree, hover highlighting, and tooltips. Best when the network is wide but not too dense.
useCases: Co-author relationships in a research database
Character interactions in a novel or screenplay
Concurrent meeting attendees across a calendar
examples: Movie cast: 25 characters, scene co-occurrence arcs

components.name: Audience Overlap
components.description: Proportional circles showing audience segment sizes and overlaps.
components.shortDescription: Audience segments drawn as proportional circles: overlaps included.
components.longDescription: Sized circles position to reveal shared membership between audience segments. Useful for ad planning, lookalike modeling, and any time 'how much of A is also in B?' is the question. Handles 2-5 segments with clean overlap geometry. Critical when planning suppression lists or measuring incremental reach.
useCases: Email subscriber overlap with paid retargeting list
examples: Newsletter, podcast, and webinar audience intersect

components.name: Animated Bar Race
components.description: Smooth animated bar chart race with interpolated transitions, watermark time labels, and customizable colors.
components.shortDescription: Animated rankings that climb, fall, and overtake: storytelling in motion.
components.longDescription: Smoothly interpolated bar chart race with a watermark time label and customizable color palette. Categories rerank frame by frame as values change over time. Built for share-worthy moments: viral on social, magnetic in keynote decks. Configurable speed, pauses, and end-state highlighting included.
useCases: Top 10 cities by population over a century
Market cap leaderboard quarter by quarter
App store rankings across a launch year

components.name: Beeswarm / Swarm Plot
components.description: Individual points placed along one axis with force-based collision so they never overlap. Reveals true record-level distribution that violin and box plots hide. Optional grouping by dimension and sizing by a second metric.
components.shortDescription: Every record gets a dot, the distribution stops hiding behind summaries.
components.longDescription: Force-based collision packs individual data points along one axis without overlap, exposing distribution shape that violin and box plots smooth away. Optional grouping by dimension and dot sizing by metric. Use when individuals matter, not just the median.
useCases: Salary distribution across 500 employees by department
Response time per request across servers
Student grades within each class section
Marathon finish times by age group
examples: Engineering salaries dotted by level, sized by tenure
Order value per transaction across 5 stores

components.name: Big Calendar
components.shortDescription: A full-month calendar grid you can pour any metric into.
components.longDescription: Familiar month-view calendar layout with day cells colored or annotated by your metric. Built for context-rich dashboards where stakeholders read by date, not by row number. Easier to scan than a table when the question is 'what happened on the 14th?'
useCases: Daily revenue across the fiscal month
Marketing send schedule with engagement counts
examples: Content publishing calendar with view counts

components.name: Bipartite Graph
components.shortDescription: Two sets, many connections, the cleanest way to map who-uses-what.
components.longDescription: Two parallel columns of nodes connected by weighted lines, designed for relationships that fit a clear A-to-B structure. Bipartite layout sidesteps hairball graphs and answers 'which customers bought which products?' or 'which authors wrote in which journals?' at a glance.
useCases: Job applicants to roles applied for
examples: Researchers to papers across a department

components.name: Break-Even Chart
components.shortDescription: Where revenue meets cost, the moment your business starts making money.
components.longDescription: Plots fixed cost, variable cost, and revenue lines against units sold, with the break-even point marked where revenue crosses total cost. The classic finance pedagogy chart, polished for executive presentations and pricing reviews. Toggle assumptions and watch the crossover slide in real time.
useCases: Pricing review for a new SaaS plan
Capacity planning for a manufacturing line
Investor pitch with break-even at 18 months
Budget approval for a launch with fixed vs variable cost split

components.name: Bubble Chart
components.shortDescription: Three dimensions, one chart: x, y, and a size that tells the third story.
components.longDescription: Classic bubble chart where each circle's position encodes two metrics and its area encodes a third. Optional category color for a fourth dimension. The most efficient way to expose patterns in mid-density datasets where simple scatter falls short. Cross-filtering and tooltip detail keep the dataset queryable.
useCases: GDP vs life expectancy with population as size
Lead score vs deal size with company headcount as size
Click-through vs conversion with spend as size
Latency vs error rate with request volume as size
examples: Country comparison: GDP × life expectancy × population

components.name: Bubble Grid
components.shortDescription: A heatmap that breathes: circles sized by metric, gridded for clarity.
components.longDescription: Two categorical axes form a grid; each cell holds a circle sized (and optionally colored) by the metric. Reads like a heatmap but communicates magnitude through area, not just hue, which the human eye decodes faster. Sorts each axis by row/column total to surface hot spots.
useCases: Test pass rate by suite × environment

components.name: Bubble Map
components.description: Packed bubble visualization where circle size encodes a metric value. Supports packed, force-directed, and grid layouts with single/gradient/series color modes, inside/outside labels, tooltips, and cross-filtering.
components.shortDescription: Bubbles packed, forced, or gridded, a flexible layout for sized data.
components.longDescription: Renders a metric as sized circles in packed, force-directed, or grid layouts. Single, gradient, or series color modes; inside or outside labels; tooltips and cross-filtering. The Swiss Army knife of 'show me magnitude across many entities'. Drop in tooltips and cross-filter for instant drill-down.
useCases: Revenue by city as packed bubbles
Followers per influencer in a campaign
Library sizes in a tech stack
examples: GitHub orgs sized by total contributors

components.name: Bullet Chart
components.shortDescription: Target, actual, and qualitative bands: KPIs without the gauge clutter.
components.longDescription: Stephen Few's bullet chart: a horizontal bar against shaded performance bands with a target marker. Replaces space-hogging gauges with a compact, comparison-friendly layout. The standard for KPI dashboards with goal context. Stack vertically for a multi-KPI scoreboard that reads in seconds.
useCases: Quarterly revenue vs target with bad/ok/good bands
examples: Q1 revenue: $4.2M actual, $4.5M target, on green

components.name: Bump Chart
components.shortDescription: Rank changes as smooth ribbons, who climbed, who slipped, who held steady.
components.longDescription: A specialty line chart where the y-axis is rank rather than value, so position shifts pop at every time step. Smooth bezier ribbons keep transitions readable even with 15+ entities. Born for leaderboards and competitive narratives. Highlight any series on hover to follow a single contender across time.
useCases: Premier League standings across a season
Top open-source projects ranked by stars

components.name: Calendar Event Heatmap
components.shortDescription: GitHub-style calendar heatmap: daily intensity at a year's glance.
components.longDescription: A year's worth of daily metric values rendered as a calendar grid colored by intensity. Reveals weekly patterns, seasonality, and outliers in seconds, the visual nobody questions. Best when daily granularity matters and density is high. Click any day to drill into the records behind the cell.
useCases: Daily order volume across a fiscal year
Daily login counts for a B2B app
examples: 365 days of contributions, intensity by commit count

components.name: Cashflow
components.description: Cashflow mirror bar chart: Income bars rise above a zero baseline, Expense bars drop below. Includes a Total Balance KPI header, legend, tooltip, cross-filtering, theme-aware colors, compact number formatting, and label-fit auto-rotation for dense time axes. 1 period dimension (e.g. month), 2 metrics (Income, Expense).
components.shortDescription: Income above the line, expenses below: cash flow you can read in one glance.
components.longDescription: Mirror bar chart for cash flow: income bars rise above a zero baseline while expense bars drop below it, with a Total Balance KPI header on top. Theme-aware colors, compact number formatting, tooltips, cross-filtering, and label auto-rotation for dense monthly axes. 1 period dimension, 2 metrics (Income, Expense).
useCases: Net balance trend with per-period detail

components.name: Choropleth Map
components.description: Tile-grid choropleth for US states or world countries. Accepts state abbreviations/names or ISO-2/ISO-3 country codes, supports sequential/diverging/binned color scales, square/rounded/hex/circle tiles, legend positioning, and cross-filtering. 1 region dimension, 1 metric, optional tooltip metric.
components.shortDescription: Tile-grid maps for US states or world countries: geography without distortion.
components.longDescription: A tile-grid choropleth that gives every region equal visual weight, so Rhode Island doesn't disappear next to Texas. Accepts state names/abbreviations or ISO-2/ISO-3 codes; supports sequential, diverging, and binned color scales with square, rounded, hex, or circle tiles.
useCases: Country-level adoption rate for a global product
Election results by state in tile form
examples: Sales by US state, sequential blue scale
World COVID case rate, diverging palette

components.name: Chord Diagram
components.description: Circular relationship diagram with arcs and ribbons connecting groups by shared values.
components.shortDescription: Every relationship traced as a ribbon, who connects to whom, in one circle.
components.longDescription: Groups arrange around a circle as labeled arcs; ribbons inside the circle connect them with width proportional to flow or shared value. Reveals dense many-to-many relationships that would be hopeless as a network graph or a bilateral matrix. Built for migration flows, trade ties, co-occurrence patterns, and any 'who connects to whom, and how strongly?' question.
useCases: Migration flows between countries or regions
Cross-team collaboration frequency in a quarterly review
examples: International student exchange flows across 12 countries

components.name: Connection Map
components.description: Entity rows with bezier arcs showing pairwise connection strength.
components.shortDescription: Entity rows linked by bezier arcs: connection strength, made visible.
components.longDescription: Rows for entities, bezier arcs spanning between them with thickness proportional to relationship strength. Less crowded than a force graph when you have a clear list and just want to surface notable pairs. Sort rows by total connection weight to bring hubs to the top.
useCases: Co-occurrence of skills across a workforce
examples: Engineering teams linked by shared on-call shifts

components.name: Conversion Heatmap
components.description: Day-of-week × hour-of-day heatmap for conversion rates or counts.
components.shortDescription: Day × hour conversion heatmap: find the moment your funnel works.
components.longDescription: A 7×24 grid colored by conversion rate or count, exposing when your audience converts versus when they vanish. Indispensable for ad scheduling, send-time optimization, and staffing decisions tied to traffic curves. Cells are clickable for drill-down into the underlying timestamps.
useCases: Find peak conversion windows for paid ads
Schedule email sends to align with engagement peaks
Plan support staffing against ticket arrival heatmap
Identify dead hours in checkout completion
examples: Support tickets opened per hour, weekday breakdown

components.name: Curved Columns (Animated + Zoom)
components.shortDescription: Animated curved columns with zoom: column charts with a softer geometry.
components.longDescription: Columns rendered with curved tops and entrance animations, plus zoom-and-pan for dense category lists. Brings polish to standard categorical comparisons when a flat bar chart feels too utilitarian. Designed for marketing dashboards and TV displays where motion earns attention.
useCases: Quarterly revenue across 30 product lines with zoom
Daily active users over 90 days, animated reveal
Top categories on a marketing dashboard
Weekly KPI summary on a TV display
examples: 52 weeks of unique visitors with zoom
Top 100 SKUs by sales, animated load

components.name: Curved Columns (Static)
components.shortDescription: Curved-top columns: categorical comparison with a softer silhouette.
components.longDescription: A standard column chart with curved column tops for visual warmth without sacrificing readability. Drop in wherever a default bar chart feels too sharp: annual reports, brand-led dashboards, executive summaries. Pair with light gridlines and minimal axes for a clean, brand-forward read.

components.name: Data Table
components.shortDescription: A data table that earns its place: sortable, dense, dashboard-ready.
components.longDescription: A polished tabular view tuned for executive dashboards: sorting, conditional formatting, inline bars, and selective column emphasis. When the audience needs the actual numbers, give them a table that respects the rest of the design. Cross-filter from any row into the rest of the dashboard.
useCases: Top 50 accounts by ARR with growth column
Inventory list with reorder threshold flags
Pipeline by stage with weighted value
Support ticket queue with priority and SLA
examples: Customer table: 100 rows × ARR, growth, NPS, churn risk
Pipeline table by stage and rep

components.name: Dependency Wheel
components.shortDescription: Dependencies arranged on a circle: every link a chord between modules.
components.longDescription: Items placed around a circle with chord ribbons connecting dependent pairs. Reveals coupling structure, hub modules, and unexpected entanglements in a way list views never could. Born for dependency maps and reciprocal flows. Hover any node to highlight its inbound and outbound chords.
useCases: Module-level coupling in a software repo
Inter-team dependencies in a quarterly plan

components.name: Chart Title
components.shortDescription: Two metrics, two axes, one chart: context without compromise.
components.longDescription: A dual-axis combo chart pairing a column metric with a line metric on a secondary scale. Use when two related-but-different-magnitude metrics belong together: revenue and margin, sessions and conversion rate, volume and price. Color and legend logic prevent the classic 'which axis is which?' confusion.
useCases: Revenue (bars) and gross margin % (line) by quarter
Sessions and conversion rate by month
Trade volume and average price by day
Tickets opened and SLA % by week

components.name: Dual Donut
components.shortDescription: Two donuts, one canvas: compare share-of-mix at a glance.
components.longDescription: Twin donut charts side by side, each tied to a different period or segment. Quickly answers 'how did our mix shift?' without forcing the viewer to flip between two slides. Ideal for before/after, plan-vs-actual, and segment comparisons. Synced legends and tooltips keep the comparison airtight.
useCases: Revenue mix this year vs last year
Customer segments: North America vs EMEA

components.name: Dumbbell Chart
components.shortDescription: Two dots, one line: change between two points, ranked top to bottom.
components.longDescription: Each row shows a category with two endpoint dots (e.g., before and after) connected by a rod, optionally colored by direction of change. The standard chart for showing magnitude and direction of change across many categories: beats grouped bars every time.
useCases: Wage gap by job title (men vs women)

components.name: Earnings (EPS) Dot Chart
components.shortDescription: EPS prints versus consensus: beats, misses, and surprise magnitude.
components.longDescription: Quarterly earnings shown as dots against analyst consensus, with surprise size encoded by deviation. Built for finance dashboards where the question 'beat, met, or missed?' must be answered for every print without scrolling. Optional surprise-percentage labels and beat/miss color coding included.
useCases: Earnings surprise dashboard for a watchlist
Sector earnings beat rate over time
examples: Last 8 quarters: EPS vs consensus, color-coded surprise
Tech sector beat rate by quarter

components.name: Engagement Heatmap
components.shortDescription: Engagement intensity mapped across two dimensions: peaks and dead zones, found.
components.longDescription: A general-purpose heatmap calibrated for engagement metrics: time on page by section, click density by feature, watch percent by chapter. Spectral or sequential color scales surface where users lean in and where they bounce. Hot-zone callouts and percentile coloring keep the eye on what matters.
useCases: Watch percent per video chapter by audience cohort
Click rate per page section by traffic source
Dwell time by article and referrer
examples: Click rate: 6 page zones × 4 acquisition channels

components.name: Flow Map
components.shortDescription: Origin-to-destination flows on a real map: geography meets movement.
components.longDescription: Curved flow lines on a base map showing volume of movement between geographic origins and destinations. Line width encodes flow magnitude. The right tool when both place and direction matter: migration, shipping lanes, traffic, money movement. Animated arrows and a basemap toggle give the map both motion and context.
useCases: Internet traffic flows between data centers
Cargo routes for a logistics carrier
examples: Container ship routes across the Atlantic

components.name: Force-Directed Network
components.shortDescription: Force-directed networks that settle into structure: clusters become obvious.
components.longDescription: Nodes repel and edges pull, simulating physics until clusters emerge naturally. Tooltips, drag, hover highlighting, and color-by-group. The classic for exploring relationship structure without imposing a layout. Tunable charge, link distance, and cluster coloring for analytical or aesthetic reads.
useCases: Co-mention graph from a media corpus
examples: 200-node Slack DM graph clustered by team

components.name: Grouped Bar Chart
components.shortDescription: Compare categories within categories, the grouped bar workhorse.
components.longDescription: Bars grouped by a primary category, with multiple sub-bars per group for comparison series. The standard for 'compare A vs B across these 10 things' when the within-group story matters as much as the across-group story. Sort within group, sort across group, or pin a benchmark series for context.
useCases: Revenue by region, split by product line
Test scores by school, split by grade
Survey responses by question, split by demographic
Hires by team, split by quarter

components.name: Hexbin Scatter
components.shortDescription: Hexagon bins where scatter goes to die: density without overlap.
components.longDescription: Aggregates dense scatter points into hexagonal bins colored by count, replacing thousands of overlapping dots with a clean tessellation. Hexagons tile space more efficiently than squares, it's why we use them. Configurable hex radius, color scale, and minimum-count threshold included.
useCases: Trade size vs price scatter (50k+ points)
Latency vs throughput scatter for backend
examples: Hexbin of 100k clicks on a 1080p screenshot
Trade volume vs price across 200k orders

components.name: Hexbin Density Plot
components.shortDescription: Hexbin tuned for density visualization: gradient fills, contour-quality.
components.longDescription: A hexbin variant emphasizing a smooth color gradient across cell counts, producing contour-like density surfaces from raw point data. When you need a dense scatter to read like a topographic map, this is the chart. Tweak bandwidth and palette to match the analytical intent.
useCases: Customer cluster density in a feature space

components.name: Interactive Globe (3D Choropleth)
components.description: Interactive 3D orthographic globe with country-level metric choropleth, drag-to-rotate, auto-spin, zoom, tooltip, and sequential colour scale. 1 country dimension, 1 metric.
components.shortDescription: An interactive 3D globe with country choropleth: drag, spin, hover, drill.
components.longDescription: Orthographic 3D globe with country-level metric coloring, drag-to-rotate, auto-spin, scroll zoom, tooltip, and a sequential color scale. Takes 1 country dimension and 1 metric: drop it on a dashboard and watch stakeholders linger. Lazy-loads geometry for fast first paint on global pages.
useCases: Hero visual on a global SaaS dashboard
Worldwide ARPU map for a board deck
examples: Country MRR with sequential blue scale
Worldwide downloads in the last 30 days

components.name: KPI Sparkline Cards
components.shortDescription: KPI cards with inline sparklines, the number, the trend, nothing else.
components.longDescription: A row of compact cards: each one shows a metric, its current value, period delta, and an inline sparkline for trend. The right answer when stakeholders ask 'just show me the numbers and where they're heading.' Color-coded delta arrows make 'up' and 'down' impossible to misread.
useCases: Top-of-dashboard KPI strip on an exec view
examples: 6-card strip: Revenue, MRR, Churn, NPS, CAC, LTV

components.name: Lollipop Chart
components.shortDescription: Bar charts on a diet, a stick and a dot say the same thing with less ink.
components.longDescription: Replaces heavy bars with a thin line and a colored dot at the value. Cleaner than a bar chart for ranking 30+ categories, and the dot draws the eye to the precise value. Tufte-approved minimalism that pairs beautifully with sparse layouts and editorial reports.
examples: Stack Overflow tags by question count

components.name: Adjacency Matrix
components.shortDescription: A network adjacency matrix: every node-pair edge in a clean grid.
components.longDescription: Each row and column is a node; each cell colors by edge presence or weight. Great for dense networks where node-link spaghetti fails, and the diagonal/block structure tells you something about clusters. Reorder rows and columns by clustering algorithm to surface community structure.
useCases: Co-occurrence of features in usage logs

components.name: Mirror Bar Chart
components.shortDescription: Two opposing bar series: population pyramids, gain/loss, head-to-head.
components.longDescription: Bars stretching left and right from a center axis, perfect for population pyramids, balance comparisons, and gain-vs-loss views. Lets two series share a single category axis without compromising readability. Optional center labels and dual-axis scaling for asymmetric distributions.
useCases: Survey agree vs disagree by question
examples: Customer wins vs churn by quarter

components.name: Multi-ring Donut
components.shortDescription: Concentric donuts that nest categories: hierarchy meets composition.
components.longDescription: Multiple concentric donut rings, each one representing a level of hierarchy or a different segmentation. Reads like a sunburst pulled apart. Cleanest way to display 2-3 hierarchical breakdowns of the same total. Hover any ring segment to highlight only its slice across the other rings.
useCases: Revenue by region (outer) by product (middle) by tier (inner)
Customer count by plan and segment
Time spent across categories at multiple granularities

components.name: Opposite Diagram
components.shortDescription: Two-sided diverging diagram: pros vs cons, gains vs losses.
components.longDescription: A two-direction diagram with categories radiating left vs right from a central axis. Built for value-versus-cost narratives, opposing forces, balance sheets, and trade-off visualizations where one chart needs to argue both sides simultaneously. Pairs naturally with decision documents and strategy reviews.
useCases: Pros vs cons of strategic options
Gains vs losses per business segment
Survey: agree vs disagree with neutral spine
examples: Strategic option A: gains and risks side by side

components.name: Parallel Coordinates Plot
components.shortDescription: Many metrics, many records, parallel axes: patterns the eye can't miss.
components.longDescription: Each record draws a polyline across parallel vertical axes (one per metric), making correlations, clusters, and outliers visually obvious. Brushing along an axis filters cross-axis instantly. The power user's multivariate explorer. Reorder axes by drag to test which arrangement makes the cluster pop.
useCases: Filter customers by combinations of metric ranges
Spot outlier servers across 8 health metrics
examples: Cars: MPG, HP, weight, 0-60, price across 50 models

components.name: Parallel Sets
components.shortDescription: Categorical parallel coords: flow ribbons across multiple dimensions.
components.longDescription: Parallel axes for categorical variables, with ribbons connecting category combinations sized by joint frequency. Reveals dominant combinations and rare ones across 3-5 dimensions of categorical data, the chart for 'who falls into which buckets together'.
examples: Titanic dataset across class, gender, age, survival

components.name: Pareto Chart
components.shortDescription: The 80/20 made visible: bars and a cumulative line, working together.
components.longDescription: Sorted bars descending with a cumulative percentage line. The classic for finding the vital few categories that drive the bulk of any metric: defects, revenue, complaints, anything where Pareto's law applies. The 80% line lands automatically and shifts as the data updates.
useCases: Top defect causes driving 80% of failures
Top SKUs driving 80% of inventory cost
examples: Customer support tickets by category, sorted with cumulative %
Defect causes in a manufacturing line

components.name: Portfolio Barcode
components.shortDescription: A barcode strip for portfolios: every holding a stripe, every signal at once.
components.longDescription: Each portfolio holding becomes a thin colored stripe, with hue or width encoding return, weight, or volatility. Ridiculously dense: fits 50+ holdings in a thumbnail. Built for trading desks and concentration-risk views. Hover any stripe to lift the holding's name, weight, and signal value.
examples: Equity portfolio of 60 holdings, stripe by daily return

components.name: Portfolio Pie Barcode
components.shortDescription: Pie composition plus barcode signals, the full portfolio fingerprint.
components.longDescription: Combines a portfolio pie chart (allocation by holding or sector) with a barcode strip below for a secondary signal: daily return, volatility, or weighted contribution. One widget, two answers, perfect for monitor-wall trading dashboards. Hover any pie slice to spotlight its barcode signal alongside.
useCases: Top 20 holdings with daily P&L stripe
examples: Equity portfolio: pie of 12 sectors + daily return strip
Top 20 holdings: weight pie + volatility strip

components.name: Progress Circles
components.shortDescription: Circular progress indicators: KPI cards that feel kinetic.
components.longDescription: A row of circular progress rings, each with a value and percent-of-goal label. Friendlier than bars for landing pages and exec summaries where the dashboard doubles as a marketing artifact and brand expression matters. Each ring animates on entrance and recalculates live as data changes.
useCases: Marketing site stats with animated rings
examples: 4 KPI rings: signups, conversion, NPS, retention

components.name: General
components.shortDescription: An area-pyramid chart: funnels and hierarchies in a tapered silhouette.
components.longDescription: A pyramid-shaped area chart where width at each level encodes magnitude. Use it for marketing funnels with strong drop-off, hierarchical levels, or any narrative where the 'narrowing' visual reinforces the data story. Stage labels and conversion percentages baked in.

components.name: Q-Q Plot
components.shortDescription: Quantile-quantile plot: does your data follow the distribution you assume?
components.longDescription: Plots theoretical quantiles vs sample quantiles to test distributional assumptions. Points hug the diagonal if the assumption holds. The first chart any data scientist reaches for when 'is this normal?' matters. Configurable theoretical distribution (normal, log-normal, exponential, custom).
useCases: Check log-normal fit for revenue distribution

components.name: Quadrant Scatter
components.shortDescription: Four quadrants, two metrics, every entity placed: strategy at a glance.
components.longDescription: A scatter divided into four quadrants by reference lines on each axis (means, medians, or thresholds). Each quadrant gets a label: 'Stars', 'Question Marks', 'Cash Cows', 'Dogs'. The strategic 2x2 framework, in chart form. Configurable axis thresholds and quadrant labels keep the framework yours.
examples: Product portfolio: market growth vs market share

components.name: Radar Chart with Data Table
components.description: Radar Chart with Data Table: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Radar chart paired with a data table: visual and exact, side by side.
components.longDescription: Combines a radar/spider chart with a synced data table beside it, so the audience gets the shape AND the precise numbers. Resolves the classic objection 'but I can't read the values off a radar chart.' Highlight a row in the table to spotlight its polygon on the radar.
useCases: Vendor evaluation across 6 criteria with table
Product feature comparison with checklist values

components.name: Radial Tree
components.shortDescription: A tree that radiates: hierarchies arranged as a circular dendrogram.
components.longDescription: Hierarchical tree laid out from center outward, with branches fanning around 360 degrees. Fits more nodes on screen than a vertical tree and makes the depth structure immediately obvious: built for org charts and taxonomies that won't fit on a slide.

components.name: Revenue Breakdown (Bar + Line Combo)
components.description: Grouped bar chart with up to 4 bar metrics and an optional line overlay (e.g. Net Margin %). Dark theme with green color scheme, legend, tooltips, cross-filtering, and a Quarterly/Annual view toggle.
components.shortDescription: Revenue bars + a margin line: composition and profitability in one view.
components.longDescription: Grouped bar chart with up to 4 revenue metrics and an optional line overlay (often Net Margin %). Dark theme, green accents, legend, tooltips, cross-filtering, and a Quarterly/Annual toggle. Built for finance review meetings. Toggle between absolute dollars and indexed view for cleaner trend reads.
useCases: Quarterly revenue mix with margin overlay
Annual revenue by segment with profitability line
examples: Annual revenue: subscription, services, hardware, other + margin

components.name: Scatter Plot with Trendline
components.description: Scatter Plot with Trendline: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Scatter plus trendline: correlation, with the line drawn for you.
components.longDescription: Two-metric scatter with an overlaid trendline (linear, polynomial, or LOESS) and optional R² annotation. The right answer when 'is there a relationship?' is the question and 'how strong is it?' is the follow-up. Optional confidence band around the trendline and outlier highlighting.
useCases: Lead score vs deal size correlation
examples: Spend vs revenue across 50 campaigns + trendline
Lead score vs ACV across 1000 deals

components.name: Semicircle Gauge
components.shortDescription: A clean semicircular gauge: one metric, one threshold, zero clutter.
components.longDescription: A 180-degree gauge with configurable color zones (red/amber/green or custom), a needle or fill indicator, and a center value. Ideal for SLA dashboards, capacity meters, and any single-number-with-context KPI. Configurable threshold lines, needle styles, and label typography.

components.name: Semi-Circle Pie Chart
components.shortDescription: Half a pie, twice the focus: composition in a wide, dashboard-friendly form.
components.longDescription: A 180-degree pie chart that fits where a circular pie would be too round. Reads cleanly in horizontal slots: KPI cards, mobile dashboards, narrow report columns. Good for 3-7 slices, and a quiet design upgrade from yet another donut. Configurable inner radius and label placement keep typography clean.
useCases: Channel mix in a sidebar widget
Status breakdown in a wide dashboard slot
Survey mix in a print-friendly layout
examples: Status breakdown: 5 categories in a sidebar
Survey response mix in a horizontal card

components.name: Simple Column Chart
components.shortDescription: The dependable column chart: categorical comparison without ceremony.
components.longDescription: Vertical bars, sortable, with optional value labels and tooltips. The chart that ships when you need a clean column chart and don't want to build it yourself. Every dashboard has at least one of these: make it a good one. Optional value labels, target lines, and conditional bar coloring.

components.name: Slice & Dice Treemap
components.description: Treemap layout that alternates horizontal and vertical splits at each level, producing an ordered grid of nested rectangles.
components.shortDescription: A treemap that respects order: every slice keeps its place, every dice keeps its rank.
components.longDescription: Unlike squarified treemaps that maximize aspect ratio, slice-and-dice alternates split direction at each hierarchy level: producing a grid that preserves data order across rows and columns. Ideal when sequence matters: time-ordered cohorts, alphabetized categories, or rank-based portfolios. Reads almost like a heatmap with hierarchical structure baked in. Click any tile to filter the rest of your dashboard.
useCases: Quarterly revenue broken down by product → region → channel
Portfolio allocation across asset classes and time horizons
Help-center traffic by article category and month
Workforce headcount across departments and seniority levels
examples: Q4 revenue: 4 product families × 6 regions, ranked by SKU count
ETF allocation: 5 asset classes × 3 risk tiers, time-ordered

components.name: Small Multiples / Trellis Grid
components.description: Small Multiples / Trellis Grid: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Trellis grid of mini-charts: one per category, all on the same scale.
components.longDescription: Small multiples lay out a mini-chart per category in a grid, all sharing axes, so visual comparison is direct. Tufte's favorite technique: the eye does pattern-finding the brain shouldn't have to compute. Configurable axes-shared mode for direct-comparison reads.
useCases: Revenue trend per region in a 4×3 grid
Per-cohort retention curves in a trellis
examples: Daily orders trended for each of 12 cities

components.name: Solid Gauge
components.shortDescription: A filled gauge that reads like a thermometer: bold, confident, single-metric.
components.longDescription: A solid-fill gauge with a center value and a fill arc proportional to the metric vs target. Bolder than a needle gauge, friendlier than a number alone. Good fit for hero KPIs and wallboards where the chart needs to register from across the room. Threshold lines and conditional fill colors respond to the metric value.
useCases: Project completion gauge for the team
OKR progress on a TV display

components.name: Stacked Area Chart
components.shortDescription: Composition that flows: stacked areas for share over time.
components.longDescription: Time on the x-axis, metric on the y, stacked layers per category showing both total and composition. Use when both 'how much' and 'made of what' need to coexist on one chart over time, and the trend in the total matters as much as the mix. Optional 100% normalization mode flips the focus from totals to share.
useCases: Revenue by product line over months
Active users by plan tier over weeks
Traffic by source over a quarter
Spend by category over a year
examples: Monthly revenue: 4 products stacked across 24 months
Daily traffic by source over 90 days

components.name: Stacked Bar Chart with Negative Values (Animated + Zoom)
components.description: Stacked Bar Chart with Negative Values (Animated + Zoom): community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Stacked bars that handle negatives: animated and zoomable.
components.longDescription: Stacked bars with proper rendering of negative values (e.g., losses below zero, gains above), plus entrance animation and zoom-and-pan. Handles the awkward 'we have both gains and losses to stack' case that breaks most charts. The chart that finally makes mixed-sign stacks comprehensible.
useCases: Quarterly P&L with gains and losses stacked
Net flows with positive and negative segments
Variance bars with offsets above and below baseline
Inventory adjustments with positive and negative entries

components.name: Stacked Bar Chart with Negative Values (Static)
components.description: Stacked Bar Chart with Negative Values (Static): community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Stacked bars that respect zero: negatives below the line, positives above.
components.longDescription: A stacked bar chart that handles mixed-sign data correctly: positive segments stack upward, negative segments stack downward, baseline at zero. The right tool for P&L breakdowns and net-flow displays. Solves a common edge case that breaks naive stacked-bar implementations. Especially valuable for finance teams who live with mixed-sign data daily.
useCases: Monthly P&L with revenue stacks above and cost stacks below zero
Variance with positive and negative components
examples: Monthly P&L: revenue + cost stacked around zero
Net flows: inflows + outflows by week

components.name: Story Flow / Narrative
components.shortDescription: Narrative flow: characters, threads, and meetings traced over time.
components.longDescription: Lines for entities (characters, accounts, contributors) that bend together when they interact and apart when they don't. A storytelling chart for narratives, project handoffs, and any 'who met whom when' analysis. Configurable line smoothing and event markers for narrative pacing.

components.name: Streamgraph
components.shortDescription: Stacked area's wilder cousin: flowing layers around a free baseline.
components.longDescription: Like stacked area, but with a moving baseline that distributes layers symmetrically (or aesthetically). Reduces the 'one layer dominates everything' problem and reads beautifully for many-category trends. Configurable baseline mode (zero, wiggle, silhouette, expand) shapes the read.
useCases: Movie genre revenue over a century

components.name: Stream Wave Chart
components.shortDescription: Streamgraph with sine-wave styling: composition that breathes.
components.longDescription: A streamgraph with smoothed wave aesthetics: extra-soft transitions, layered transparency, and editorial polish. Same data shape as a standard streamgraph, but tuned for design-conscious dashboards and reports. A choice when the data deserves a chart that feels as designed as the story.
useCases: Trend story on a news site
examples: 10 product categories' share, 5-year trend, editorial style

components.name: Sunburst Chart
components.shortDescription: Concentric rings of hierarchy: composition at every level, all at once.
components.longDescription: Hierarchical part-to-whole shown as concentric rings: center is total, outer rings are deeper levels. Click to zoom into a slice. Reads complex hierarchies in seconds: drill structure built in, and the layout scales gracefully to four or five levels.
useCases: File system size by folder hierarchy
Org breakdown by division → department → team

components.name: Time Series with Annotations
components.description: Time Series with Annotations: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: A time series that knows context: value lines plus event annotations.
components.longDescription: Standard time series with annotation markers for events (launches, incidents, campaigns), plus tooltip details and configurable axes. The right baseline for any line chart that needs 'why did the number jump on April 14?' answered. Annotation markers are clickable, with deep-link support to the source event.
useCases: MRR trend with pricing change markers
Stock price with earnings event flags

components.name: Traffic Sources Chord
components.shortDescription: Traffic sources as a chord diagram: channels and their crossover paths.
components.longDescription: A chord diagram showing channel-to-channel traffic flows, where users move between sources before converting. Reveals the path complexity that linear funnels hide, exposing every cross-channel handoff that shaped the final attribution. Hover any chord to isolate the source-target pair from the rest of the flow.

components.name: Zoomable Treemap
components.shortDescription: A treemap that drills: click any tile to dive into its hierarchy.
components.longDescription: Hierarchical part-to-whole as nested rectangles sized by metric, with click-to-zoom drill-down. Best for budget breakdowns, file system displays, and any 'what's inside this big block?' analysis where the audience expects to explore. Breadcrumb navigation lets viewers reach any depth without losing context.
useCases: Budget breakdown with click-through to line items
File system size with folder drill-down
Spend by vendor with invoice drill
Revenue by region with country drill

components.name: Variable-Radius Nested Donut
components.shortDescription: Concentric donuts where each ring scales: magnitude meets composition.
components.longDescription: Nested donut rings where ring radius is variable per ring (encoding total magnitude) while slice arcs encode composition. Two dimensions of information in a single radial widget: magnitude AND mix, without sending the audience to two charts. Synced legend and tooltips tie the magnitude and mix together cleanly.
examples: Department mix per year, radius = total headcount

components.name: Variance Bar
components.shortDescription: Variance bars that show actual vs plan: over and under, color-coded.
components.longDescription: Bars per category showing variance from a baseline (plan, prior period, target) with color encoding direction. Replaces the awkward 'two bars side by side' pattern with a clean delta visualization that highlights gaps and surpluses immediately. Optional reference line and percentage labels for executive-ready reads.
useCases: Plan vs actual variance per business unit
Budget vs spend variance per category
Forecast vs actual variance per quarter

components.name: Variable Radius Pie Chart
components.description: Variable Radius Pie Chart: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Pie slices with variable radii, a second metric without a second chart.
components.longDescription: A pie chart where each slice has both an arc (encoding share) AND a variable radius (encoding a second metric like growth or margin). Two dimensions in one figure: power-user composition that rewards a closer look from your audience. Configurable radius range and palette keep the second metric visually disciplined.
examples: Revenue mix with growth rate as radius

components.name: Title
components.shortDescription: Waffle charts: proportions as a 10×10 grid that anyone can read.
components.longDescription: A 10×10 (or N×N) grid of squares where each square is one percent of the whole. More accurate than a pie for small-difference comparisons and far more accessible to general audiences. Beloved by editorial and infographic designers. A more honest pie alternative that keeps small percentages visually present.
useCases: Survey response breakdown for an editorial piece

components.name: Wind Rose / Polar Bar
components.description: Wind Rose / Polar Bar: community visualization.
components.shortDescription: Polar bars that read like a compass: direction and magnitude together.
components.longDescription: Bars radiating outward from center on a 360-degree compass, with length encoding magnitude per direction. Born for wind data, but equally home with any directional metric: bearings, hours of day, or 12-month cycles. Configurable bin count, baseline, and color scale for editorial control.
useCases: Wind speed by direction at a weather station
Activity by hour of day in polar form
examples: Activity by hour of day, radial

components.name: Word / Tag Cloud
components.shortDescription: Word clouds that don't look terrible: sized by frequency, hand-tuned typography.
components.longDescription: Words sized by frequency and laid out without overlap, with attention to typography and palette so the result reads as a designed object rather than the default cloud. Best for editorial summaries and feedback comprehension. Optional sentiment coloring and exclusion lists for cleaner output.
useCases: Top trending tags from a month of content
Brand mention cloud from social listening
examples: Trending tags from a content month

components.name: Year-over-Year Line
components.description: Year-over-Year line chart: current vs prior year overlay with optional shaded delta.
components.shortDescription: Current vs prior year on one axis, with the gap shaded so wins stand out.
components.longDescription: Year-over-year line chart that overlays the current period on the prior year with an optional shaded delta band between them. Instantly shows where this year is ahead or behind, with tooltips, theme-default colors, and cross-filtering.
useCases: Compare revenue to last year by week or month
Report YoY growth without a calc field
